businessId.meta.title: What is a Business ID? — BlockID.au
businessId.meta.description: A Business ID bundles verified identity, evidence and capabilities into one reusable record. Five verification levels, 13-area analysis, consent-based sharing.
businessId.headline: One Business. One Trusted Identity.
businessId.subhead: A Business ID is a verified digital identity that carries your evidence, verification level and capabilities — so investors, procurement teams and grant panels can trust what you claim, without re-verifying it every time.
businessId.what.title: What a Business ID is
businessId.what.intro: Four ingredients bundled into one reusable record — verified once, presented on your terms, revocable at any time.
businessId.what.identity.title: Verified identity
businessId.what.identity.body: ASIC/ABR/ABN checked, directors matched, domain and email owner confirmed. The identity anchor for everything else on your profile.
businessId.what.evidence.title: Evidence
businessId.what.evidence.body: Traction, financials, contracts, IP — stored encrypted, hash-anchored in an audit log, cited inline in your Trust Report.
businessId.what.capabilities.title: Capabilities
businessId.what.capabilities.body: What your business can actually do — sector, offering, team skills, tooling — scored on the 13-area rubric.
businessId.what.reusable.title: Reusable
businessId.what.reusable.body: One record, many share packages. Send a signed link to an investor today, a buyer tomorrow, a grant panel next week — always current, never re-typed.
businessId.levels.title: Five verification levels
businessId.levels.intro: Each level adds a checkable claim on top of the previous one. Public /id/{slug} profiles surface the badge for the level you have reached.
businessId.level1.title: L1 — Self-declared
businessId.level1.body: You have created a Business ID with a name, jurisdiction hint and email. Not sufficient for a public profile.
businessId.level2.title: L2 — Identity verified
businessId.level2.body: ASIC/ABR/ABN record matched, domain ownership confirmed, email owner verified. Minimum bar for a public /id/{slug} profile.
businessId.level3.title: L3 — Financials attested
businessId.level3.body: Financial statements attested by a qualified accountant (CA/CPA/IPA in AU, equivalent overseas). Practical bar for investor and procurement diligence.
businessId.level4.title: L4 — Independently audited
businessId.level4.body: Financial statements audited by an independent registered auditor. Required for Series A+ diligence and material procurement contracts.
businessId.level5.title: L5 — Cross-jurisdictional
businessId.level5.body: Evidence and verification present in a second jurisdiction (used by the AU-VN corridor cohort). Includes DKKD/MST alongside ASIC/ABR.
businessId.pillars.title: 13-area analysis — 4 pillars
businessId.pillars.intro: The same 13-area rubric applies to every Business ID. Investors compare apples with apples; founders know exactly which areas need evidence.
businessId.pillar1.title: Leadership & People
businessId.pillar1.a2: Culture, org design and hiring pipeline
businessId.pillar2.title: Strategy & Commercial
businessId.pillar3.title: Ops & Performance
businessId.pillar4.title: Tech & Digital
businessId.sharing.title: How sharing works
businessId.sharing.consent.title: Consent-based
businessId.sharing.consent.body: Nothing on your Business ID leaves your control unless you create a share package. Each package selects specific evidence and audiences.
businessId.sharing.expiry.title: Time-limited
businessId.sharing.expiry.body: Every share link carries an expiry (default 30 days). Recipients see a countdown. After expiry, the link 404s — no accidental long tails.
businessId.sharing.revocation.title: Revocable, audited
businessId.sharing.revocation.body: Revoke instantly at any time. Every view is logged with timestamp, IP, and (if the viewer is signed in) their Business ID — hash-chained for tamper evidence.
businessId.badge.title: Badge widget
businessId.badge.intro: Embed your verified badge on your website, LinkedIn or email signature. Renders your current verification level, last update date, and a link to your public /id/{slug} profile — updates in real time when your level changes.
businessId.badge.caption: Sample badge: Verified Business ID · Level 3 · updated Jul 2026. Copy the embed snippet from your dashboard.
businessId.cta.title: Create Your Business ID
businessId.disclaimer: Nothing on this page is financial or legal advice. Verification confirms what the record says, not the underlying business decision. Auschain PTY LTD · ACN 659 615 111 · ABN 79 659 615 111 · Sydney NSW.

meta.solutions.investor.title: For investors — one score across 8 dimensions, backed by the startup's own evidence | BlockID.au
meta.solutions.investor.description: Screen an Australian startup in minutes on the same 8-dimension, 13-criteria rubric, reviewed by 11 C-Level agents and an auditor, valued in AUD, and re-scored every week. Pay per report or start a 7-day free trial on Scout.
solutions.investor.headline: One score across 8 investor dimensions, backed by the startup's own evidence — screen a deal in minutes and watch it move every week.
solutions.investor.persona: Add a startup you are evaluating. BlockID scores it on the same 8 dimensions and 13 criteria it applies to every company, runs the whole C-suite of 11 agents over its evidence, audits the claims, and re-scores it as the company changes — so a first pass compares like with like, and the second pass is already waiting.
solutions.investor.benefits.title: Why an investor uses BlockID instead of a deck and a prompt
solutions.investor.benefit1.title: One rubric for every deal
solutions.investor.benefit1.body: 8 dimensions × 13 criteria × 12 growth phases, scored the same way for every startup in your pipeline. Scores are comparable across companies, each judgement carries its reasoning, and you can disagree with one line rather than with the whole number.
solutions.investor.benefit2.title: A whole C-suite reviews each startup
solutions.investor.benefit2.body: 11 C-Level agents — CFO valuation, CLO legal with ESIC and s708, CMO market, CRO funding readiness, CTO, CHRO and more — each with its own domain module and Australian context. Then an auditor checks the claims and flags what the evidence does not support.
solutions.investor.benefit3.title: The startup's own evidence, accumulating
solutions.investor.benefit3.body: Evidence vault, weekly SVI snapshots, score history and data room: the company updates itself and you see the delta, without waiting for a founder email. Your data belongs to your startup. We store it so every report builds on your own evidence and the AI reasons on your case. Founder-consented access tiers control who sees what.
solutions.investor.faq.title: Frequently asked
solutions.investor.faq.a1: A full Trust BizReport on a startup you enter: the 8-dimension, 13-criteria score with its reasoning, an AUD valuation range with the methods shown, the C-suite review, the auditor's flags and a next-step plan, as a PDF. No subscription needed, and an ATO tax invoice on the charge.
solutions.investor.faq.a2: Scout ({scoutPrice} a month) includes {scoutReports} reports a month, {scoutStartups} tracked startups, a weekly Progress Radar with score deltas, stage changes and new evidence, deal-flow browse and a watchlist. Firm ({firmPrice}) and Program ({programPrice}) add seats, white-label reports and cohort tools. Every plan starts with a 7-day free trial, card required — nothing is billed if you cancel before day 7.
solutions.investor.faq.q3: Is a score a substitute for diligence?
solutions.investor.faq.a3: No. It is a triage layer built from what the founder gave us and what is publicly available, audited for unsupported claims. Nothing on the platform is financial or investment advice, and every decision remains yours.
solutions.investor.disclaimer: Not financial, investment or legal advice. Scores and valuation ranges are generated from founder-supplied and publicly available information; investment decisions remain your own. Auschain PTY LTD · ACN 659 615 111 · ABN 79 659 615 111 · Sydney NSW.

meta.solutions.accelerator.description: Score every startup in a cohort on the same 8-dimension, 13-criteria rubric, reviewed by 11 C-Level agents and an auditor, then show sponsors the progress. Program plan with a 7-day free trial; multi-cohort programs talk to us.
solutions.accelerator.eyebrow: For accelerators, incubators and university programs
solutions.accelerator.headline: Score the whole cohort on one rubric, then show sponsors the progress — automatically.
solutions.accelerator.persona: Every startup in your program is scored on the same 8 dimensions and 13 criteria across 12 growth phases, reviewed by 11 C-Level agents with an auditor behind them, and re-scored as it changes — so the cohort compares like with like and sponsors see movement, not memory.
solutions.accelerator.benefits.title: What a program gets
solutions.accelerator.benefit1.title: One rubric across the whole cohort
solutions.accelerator.benefit1.body: 8 dimensions × 13 criteria × 12 growth phases, applied the same way to every company you take in, so two startups side by side is a real comparison. Batch scoring queues a whole application round or cohort on one rubric — with your own weights across the 8 dimensions if you want them — scores it off-peak overnight, and lands in a cohort table you can sort and download as CSV.
solutions.accelerator.benefit2.title: A C-suite review for every founder
solutions.accelerator.benefit2.body: 11 C-Level agents review each startup — valuation, legal and ESIC, market, funding readiness, tech, team — with an auditor flagging unsupported claims. Your mentors start from a diligence-grade read instead of a deck.
solutions.accelerator.benefit3.title: Progress you can show, company by company
solutions.accelerator.benefit3.body: Each startup's evidence accumulates and its score is re-taken weekly, so movement between sessions is visible and a sponsor update is assembled from the record rather than from memory. Your data belongs to your startup. We store it so every report builds on your own evidence and the AI reasons on your case. Founder-consented access tiers control who sees what.
solutions.accelerator.journey.title: What a cohort's first 90 days look like
solutions.accelerator.journey.step1.head: Set the cohort up
solutions.accelerator.journey.step1.b1: Add every startup in the cohort and run its first score on the shared rubric.
solutions.accelerator.journey.step1.b2: Assign mentors — roster, check-ins and notes sit beside the score.
solutions.accelerator.journey.step1.b3: Read the gaps the first scores name across the whole cohort.
solutions.accelerator.journey.step2.head: Work the gaps
solutions.accelerator.journey.step2.b1: Run sessions against the dimensions the cohort scores worst on.
solutions.accelerator.journey.step2.b2: Fill each company's data room in the order investors ask for it.
solutions.accelerator.journey.step2.b3: Re-run the scores and compare them against the first pass.
solutions.accelerator.journey.step3.head: Demo day
solutions.accelerator.journey.step3.b1: Each founder shares a live investor link instead of a PDF.
solutions.accelerator.journey.step3.b2: Publish the founders who consent to a public profile at /listings/{slug}.
solutions.accelerator.journey.step3.b3: Export the sponsor / LP report for the cohort from the cohort table.
solutions.accelerator.faq.title: Frequently asked
solutions.accelerator.faq.q1: Can we score a whole cohort in one run?
solutions.accelerator.faq.a1: Yes. Tick the startups in your evaluations workspace, choose Batch score, name the round and optionally set rubric weights for the 8 dimensions. Every company gets a full Trust BizReport on the same rubric, scored off-peak overnight from your plan's included reports, and you get a sortable cohort table — SVI, weighted score, stage, movement since last score, top strength and top gap per startup — plus a CSV export.
solutions.accelerator.faq.q2: Can our sponsors or LPs see the underlying startups?
solutions.accelerator.faq.a2: Only what you or the founder chooses to share — founder-consented access tiers control who sees what. Program includes a packaged sponsor / LP report per cohort: cover, cohort summary (size, median SVI, movers), a one-line read on each startup, and the methodology and disclaimers, exported from the cohort table and ready to print or save as PDF.
solutions.accelerator.faq.q3: How does pricing work for a program?
solutions.accelerator.faq.a3: Program is {programPrice} a month — {programReports} reports, {programStartups} tracked startups, {programSeats} seats — with a 7-day free trial, card required. Any startup you enter can also be reported on pay-as-you-go for {reportPrice}. Multi-cohort accelerators, and programs that need more seats, SSO or white-label reports, talk to us through Contact Sales.

compare.fair.1.body: Code, architecture, debugging, documentation. A general model is a very good engineer at your elbow.
compare.fair.2.title: Drafting
compare.fair.2.body: Investor updates, memos, policies, cold emails. Give it your facts and it writes the first version faster than anyone.

compare.faq.q2: When do I still need an independent valuer?
compare.faq.a2: For anything that has to stand on its own in a transaction, a dispute, a tax matter or a court: a share buy-back, a family-law settlement, an employee share scheme valuation for the ATO, an expert report. A Trust BizReport is a screening and tracking instrument, not a formal valuation, and it says so on every page.
compare.faq.q3: Is a Trust BizReport a substitute for due diligence?
compare.faq.a3: No. It is a triage layer built from what the founder supplied and what is publicly available, audited for unsupported claims. It tells you where to look; it does not replace the looking. Nothing on the platform is financial, investment or legal advice.

compare.sources.title: Sources
compare.sources.intro: Cited by name, not linked. Prices are published list prices as of September 2026.
compare.sources.1: developmentcorporate.com (2026) — general models give systematically different verdicts on identical decks (GPT-4o vs Claude) and hallucinate founder histories, competitors and market figures; 85% of VCs use AI daily, 12% with a governed workflow.
compare.sources.2: MicroVentures — AI can hallucinate or invent facts, carries confirmation bias, and gives limited information on how it reached a conclusion; use it only with human intervention.
compare.sources.3: VC Lab (July 2026) — general models can confidently produce wrong information; do not upload confidential documents without checking the data policy.
compare.sources.4: VCBench, arXiv 2509.14448 — language models beat human precision only when given a consistent, anonymised rubric.
compare.sources.5: Multi-agent VC due-diligence framework, arXiv 2605.13110 — single-prompt language models lack role separation and evidence tracing.
compare.sources.prices: Price anchors — professionalbusinessvaluers.com.au (startup valuation from A$2,985 inc GST); abva.com.au (A$3,990 + GST); equidam.com (Advanced US$412, Expert US$1,063); valutico.com (about US$7,000 a year); kruncher.com (US$499 a month, about US$5 an analysis); crunchbase.com (Pro US$49 a month); affinity.co (US$2,000–2,700 a seat a year); openai.com (ChatGPT Plus US$20 a month; Enterprise about US$45–75 a seat with a roughly 150-seat minimum); perplexity.ai (Enterprise US$40 a seat).
